answer: Each identity must post a 500-token bond plus a hardware credential, and the cipher signed by that device anchors the bond to one agent. An attacker forging N identities locks 500N tokens, and a proven sybil claim slashes 100% of every linked bond after a 30-epoch wait. Splitting identities multiplies the marginal cost per fake, while the shared penalty and independent jurors catch any ocean of copies before the shale of duplicate credentials passes review.
